citation: Pedersen et al., The Martini 3 Lipidome: Expanded and Refined Parameters Improve Lipid Phase Behavior, ACS Central Science (2025)

vendored.ITPs/: the parameter files themselves, all of them: the bonded-term lookup reads every ITP under references/, so committing only the three files a pdc topology includes would make a fresh clone match fewer terms than this checkout does
vendored.README.md: the upstream note that states the DOI and the citation

not_vendored..git-upstream/: the upstream checkout, renamed from `.git`: a nested `.git` makes git treat the whole directory as an embedded repository, so the parameter files could not be tracked at all. Renaming it preserves the checkout and its history; rename it back to `.git` to pull upstream updates.

used_by.pdc topologies: martini_v3.0.0.itp (bead types), martini_v3.0.0_solvents_v1.itp (water as W), martini_v3.0.0_ions_v1.itp (NA, CL): copied into each run and named in its manifest
used_by.bonded-term lookup: every ITP here, so a mapping's terms can match a published Martini 3 value -- which is how the DDM tail stopped falling back to placeholders

caveat: The detergent built from this set is a first draft, by the user's decision: the parameters are published, but the mapping that assigns beads to atoms, and therefore which published terms apply, is ours and is not yet validated against an atomistic reference.
